text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT [INC-2026-0429] p99 generation latency exceeded threshold on /v1/generate (model=redwood-2, region=us-east-1). threshold 900ms, observed 1450ms. link: https://monitoring.redwood/prod/INC-2026-0429

maria: paging oncall. aj you're primary until 15:00PT, correct? I'll put a brief summary here.

aj: I am primary until 15:00PT and can start triage. Initial check: error rate stable, qps steady, but tail latency up. Not seeing increased 5xx.

sasha: I'm secondary and available to take over at handoff. There's an overnight coverage hole from 02:00-03:30 UTC tonight we still need to fill.

kevin: infra-oncall here. No host reboots in last hour. Network shows increased retransmits between AZ-1 and AZ-3 at :10 and :12. Could be packet drops causing retries.

leila (runtime-oncall): joining. I pulled traces and see frequent KV cache evictions and sporadic larger batch sizes for some customers. Also some requests with very long system context. Can we get a sanitized example?

aj: sanitized example pasted:
```
{"prompt": "[REDACTED LONG SYSTEM MESSAGE]\n[user history x20 entries]", "max_new_tokens": 3000, "temperature": 0.2}
```

leila: that explains heavy attention/tokens. Options: 1) temporarily route those heavy-context customers to hi-mem pool; 2) apply a soft per-route token cap enforcement; 3) enable aggressive KV prewarming. For immediate mitigation we recommend (1).

kevin: infra can add a temporary routing rule to tag traffic from the affected customer IDs -> pool=hi-mem-us-east-1. That will increase cost but should bring p99 down quickly. We need runtime to confirm compatibility with hi-mem instances.

leila: hi-mem is compatible. Please also enable debug traces on 10 sample requests so we can confirm KV hit improvement.

omar (security-oncall): from sec side, no auth anomalies. If routing change requires an ACL update we need a quick ticket for audit, but emergency core routing changes are allowed under the oncall emergency policy. I'll stand by for the audit note.

kevin: applied route change id=r-90112. Starting to shift traffic now, estimated full weight in ~60s. https://routing.redwood/changes/r-90112

incident-bot: :repeat: Routing change r-90112 deployed. Monitor: https://monitoring.redwood/prod/INC-2026-0429/graph

leila: initial metrics: subset routed shows p99 ~540ms, overall p99 trending to 760ms. KV cache hit ratio on routed subset improved from 47% -> 89%.

tom-support: drafting customer notice. Proposed: "We've applied a temporary routing change to reduce latency for some generation requests in us-east-1. You may still see intermittent delays for long-context requests while we monitor. If you want proactive mitigation for specific customer IDs, please attach the IDs and we can prioritize." Want it posted to status.redwood.com?

maria: yes post as "degraded performance" not outage. Keep messaging tight. Also add a link to the support contact for customers with business impact.

aj: runbook link we used: https://docs.redwood/internal/runbooks/latency-spikes. Action items to add: detection rule for long-context bursts, automatic soft token caps, and explicit approval flow for emergency route changes (runtime->infra apply -> security notified -> support notified).

sasha: two notes for handoff: 1) aj will remain primary until 15:00PT and then hand off to sasha; 2) if p99 creeps back above 1s after rollback of the route, escalate to infra for packet-level analysis and to security for audit of any unusual traffic patterns.

kevin: quick FYI on rollback criteria: we should keep the route in place until p99 < 900ms for 10m after traffic normalizes. Rolling back earlier is risky.

leila: agreed. Also will add a short-lived metric alert to detect batch-size increases beyond historical 99th percentile so we catch regressions faster.

maria: coverage gap reminder. sasha please open a follow-up thread in #oncall-scheduling to collect volunteers for 02:00-03:30 UTC. We should document a mini-handoff checklist for night coverage.

omar: adding security note: when infra applies route changes, include a minimal audit comment with the change explaining incident id and approver. I'll add this to the ATO doc.

aj: handoff checklist (I'll paste to incident tracker): mitigation applied (r-90112), debug traces on 10 samples, KV metrics improved, support notice posted, runtime/infra/sec agreed rollback criteria. I'm staying on for another 30m of watch then handing to sasha.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: update logged INC-2026-0429 status=mitigated-subset.

sasha: I have the watch. I'll post a 15m status update and then clear if stable. Thanks team. Great coordination. :thumbsup:

maria: filing action items: 1) add long-context detection to runbook (owner: runtime team), 2) define emergency route approval flow in runbooks (owner: infra + sec), 3) schedule volunteer coverage for overnight (owner: oncall-scheduling).

aj: last metric check before handoff: p99 = 710ms overall, routed subset = 530ms. handing off now. first_message_ts=1825104321 last_message_ts=1825106120

sasha: confirmed. taking primary. I'll keep this thread as the escalation hub if things regress.
